stem: Which process asks whether there is a viable and worthwhile project?
options: Initiating a project
Starting up a project
Directing a project
Managing a stage boundary
explanation: Starting up a project makes sure the prerequisites for initiating a project are in place by answering whether there is a viable and worthwhile project. The decision to start must be explicit.

stem: What is the organizational ecosystem?
options: The business, user and supplier groups on the project board
The people assigned to roles in the project management team
The users who will operate the project's products after handover to business as usual
An organization's internal elements together with its external relationships
explanation: The organizational ecosystem is the internal elements of an organization (staff, board, owners) together with its external relationships such as customers, partners, suppliers, regulators and competitors.

stem: What is the purpose of the organizing practice?
options: To define and establish the project's structure of accountability
To judge whether the project remains desirable and viable
To compare actual achievements against those planned
To document the user's requirements and how they will be met during the project
explanation: The organizing practice defines and establishes the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities, the 'who'. Documenting requirements is the quality practice; comparing actuals with plans is progress.

stem: Halfway through a project, a competitor launches a cheaper product and the expected sales benefits fall below the project's costs. Which principle says the project should now be stopped?
options: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Ensure continued business justification
Learn from experience
Focus on products
explanation: Ensure continued business justification requires a justification for the investment to start the project and throughout it. If the project is no longer justified, it should be stopped. Manage by exception concerns tolerances and escalation.

stem: What is the purpose of the business case practice?
options: To judge whether the project is and remains desirable, viable and achievable
To identify, assess and control uncertainties affecting the project objectives
To define the products and the means to deliver them
To collect issues and control changes to the baseline
explanation: The business case practice establishes mechanisms to judge whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable, to support decisions on continued investment. Controlling uncertainty is the risk practice.

stem: What is the purpose of the plans practice?
options: To identify, assess and control the project's risks
To compare actual progress with what was planned
To set the structure of accountability for the project
To define the products and the means to deliver them
explanation: The plans practice facilitates communication and control by defining the products to be delivered (the what) and the means to deliver them (who, how, where, when and how much), to satisfy the business case (the why).

stem: What is the purpose of the quality practice?
options: To check that the project remains desirable, viable and achievable
To document user requirements and establish how they will be met
To control changes to the products in the project baseline
To define who is accountable for each product
explanation: The quality practice documents the user's requirements of the project products and establishes the means by which they will be met.

stem: What is the purpose of the risk practice?
options: To collect issues and control changes to the baseline
To forecast the project's objectives and its continued viability
To judge whether the project remains worth doing
To identify, assess and control uncertainties affecting objectives
explanation: The risk practice identifies, assesses and controls uncertainties that would affect the project's objectives, improving the project's ability to succeed.

stem: What is the purpose of the issues practice?
options: To document user requirements and how they will be met
To collect and assess issues and control changes to the baseline
To monitor actual achievements against those planned
To identify, assess and control the uncertainties affecting the project
explanation: The issues practice collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the project's baseline. In PRINCE2, issue management encompasses change control.

stem: Which is part of the purpose of the progress practice?
options: To define the structure of accountability
To judge whether the project is desirable
To document the user's quality requirements for products
To control any deviations causing an exception
explanation: The progress practice monitors and compares actual achievements against plans, forecasts the project's objectives and continued viability, and controls any deviations causing an exception.

stem: What is the purpose of directing a project?
options: To assign work, monitor it and take corrective action to keep the stage within tolerance
To let the board be accountable through key decisions, delegating daily management
To control the link between the project manager and the team manager
To set solid foundations before committing significant resources
explanation: Directing a project enables the project board to be accountable for success by making key decisions and exercising overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager.

stem: Which describes a stakeholder in PRINCE2?
options: Anyone who must approve a product before it is handed over to the users
Anyone who holds a named role in the project management team
Anyone who can affect, is affected by, or feels affected by the project
Anyone who has paid for part of the project's budget
explanation: A stakeholder is any individual, group or organization that can affect or be affected by, or perceives itself to be affected by, the project. Many stakeholders have no formal role.

stem: Which list gives the five integrated elements of PRINCE2?
options: Principles, practices, processes, products, tolerances
People, plans, processes, products, project board
Principles, people, practices, processes, project context
Principles, practices, processes, stages and the project board
explanation: PRINCE2 7 has five integrated elements: the principles, people, the practices, the processes and the project context. Products, stages and tolerances are concepts used inside the method, not elements of it.

stem: Which three interests does PRINCE2 represent on the project board?
options: Executive, manager and team
Business, customer and sponsor
User, supplier and regulator
Business, user and supplier
explanation: PRINCE2 focuses on three stakeholder interests, business, user and supplier, represented on the board by the executive, the senior user and the senior supplier.

stem: Which process establishes solid foundations so the business understands the work before committing significant expenditure?
options: Controlling a stage
Starting up a project
Managing product delivery
Initiating a project
explanation: Initiating a project establishes solid foundations, so the business understands the work needed to deliver the project product before committing significant expenditure or resources.

stem: Before a new project starts, the project manager reads the lessons reports of two similar projects. Which principle is being applied?
options: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Learn from experience
Manage by stages
Tailor to suit the project
explanation: Learn from experience means the team seeks, records and applies lessons from earlier projects and throughout the project, and shares them for others. Reading earlier lessons reports at the start is a direct use of it.

stem: A new online booking system goes live. Customers now book without phoning, and call costs fall by 15%. What is the fall in call costs?
options: A benefit
An outcome
An output
A capability
explanation: The system is the output, customers booking online is the outcome (the result of the change), and the measurable improvement in call costs is the benefit that contributes to a business objective.

stem: Which plan is the detailed basis for project management control throughout a stage?
options: Project plan
Team plan
Exception plan
Stage plan
explanation: A stage plan is a detailed plan used as the basis for project management control throughout a stage. The project plan is high level, and a team plan covers one work package.

stem: What are acceptance criteria?
options: The quality measures applied by reviewers to each specialist product in every stage of the project
The standards the supplier uses to build its specialist products
The checks the project board makes before authorizing a stage
A prioritized list of criteria the project product must meet for the user to accept it
explanation: Acceptance criteria are a prioritized list of criteria that the project product must meet before the user will accept it. Quality measures applied by those doing quality control are quality specifications.

stem: Who is the risk owner?
options: The person who carries out an agreed action in response to a risk
The person assigned to take responsibility for responding to a risk
The project board member whose budget or area of concern the risk affects
The person who first identified the risk and recorded it
explanation: The risk owner is assigned to take responsibility for responding to a risk. The risk action owner, also called the risk actionee, carries out an agreed response action.

stem: A user asks for an extra report to be added to a system whose specification has already been approved. What type of issue is this?
options: A request for change
A business opportunity
A problem
An off-specification
explanation: A request for change is a proposal for a change to a baseline, here the approved specification. An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications.

stem: Which report does the project manager send to the project board at agreed intervals during a stage?
options: End stage report
Checkpoint report
Exception report
Highlight report
explanation: A highlight report is a time-driven report from the project manager to the board on stage progress. Checkpoint reports go from a team manager to the project manager.

stem: Why is change management important on a PRINCE2 project?
options: Change management replaces the need for a business case
Projects deliver change that affects people's business as usual
It is needed only when the project brings in an external supplier
It controls changes to the approved project baseline
explanation: Change management is the means by which an organization moves from the current state to the target state. Projects deliver change that affects people's routines and responsibilities. Controlling changes to the baseline is change control, part of the issues practice.

stem: Which is an objective of controlling a stage?
options: The project is closed in an orderly way
The project brief is assembled
Work on products allocated to the team is authorized
Risks and issues are kept under control
explanation: Controlling a stage keeps attention on delivering the stage's products, controls risks and issues, keeps the business case under review and keeps delivery within tolerances. Authorizing team work is an objective of managing product delivery.

stem: Which statement about the executive is correct?
options: The executive represents the users who will operate the products
There can be several, one for each part of the business affected
The role can be delegated to the project manager on a small or low-risk project
There is only one, and the role cannot be combined with the project manager
explanation: The executive is the single point of accountability for the project, and this accountability cannot be delegated. There cannot be more than one executive, and the role cannot be combined with that of the project manager.

stem: What is the difference between leadership and management in PRINCE2?
options: Leadership motivates people; management instructs tasks in agreed ways
Leadership sets tolerances; management reports against them
Leadership is the project board's job; management is the team manager's job
Leadership applies to suppliers; management applies to users
explanation: Leadership is motivating people to achieve the project's objectives, best done through collaboration and influence. Management is instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working. Every role needs some of both.

stem: The project board sets limits of time and cost for a stage and only expects to be involved if the project manager forecasts that they will be exceeded. Which principle does this show?
options: Tailor to suit the project
Manage by stages
Ensure continued business justification
Manage by exception
explanation: Manage by exception sets limits of delegated authority as tolerances against plans. The board then intervenes only when a forecast says a tolerance will be exceeded. Manage by stages is about planning and controlling stage by stage.

stem: What is a dis-benefit?
options: A cost that was left out of the business case
A benefit that is realized later than planned
A risk that would have a negative effect on business objectives
A measurable decline from an outcome seen as negative
explanation: A dis-benefit is the measurable decline resulting from an outcome perceived as negative by the investing organization, which detracts from business objectives. A risk is uncertain; a dis-benefit is an expected result.

stem: What is the starting point of PRINCE2 product-based planning?
options: Defining and analysing the required products
Estimating the cost of each activity
Preparing the schedule and the resource levels
Agreeing the tolerances for the plan
explanation: Product-based planning starts by defining and analysing the products needed, then derives the work breakdown, estimates and schedule from the product descriptions.

stem: Which statement about quality assurance is correct?
options: It is typically managed independently of the project team
It is carried out by the producer of each specialist product
It is recorded only in the daily log
It replaces quality control on smaller projects
explanation: Quality assurance is a planned, systematic activity that gives confidence products will meet their quality specifications. It is typically managed independently of the project team, often by the business.

stem: A project insures its equipment against damage, so that a third party pays for any loss. Which risk response is this?
options: Avoid
Reduce
Transfer
Accept
explanation: Transferring a risk passes part of its impact, often the financial part, to a third party, as insurance does. Avoiding removes the threat, reducing lowers its probability or impact, and accepting takes no action.

stem: A team member reports a minor concern that the project manager can handle informally. Where should it be recorded?
options: In the risk register
In the daily log
In an issue report
In the issue register
explanation: The daily log records problems and concerns that the project manager can handle informally. The issue register and issue reports are for issues managed formally.

stem: Which is an example of an event-driven control?
options: A fortnightly team progress meeting
A weekly checkpoint report from a team
An end stage report at the end of a stage
A monthly highlight report to the project board
explanation: Event-driven controls happen when a specific event occurs, such as the end of a stage, completion of the PID or an exception report. Regular reports at set intervals are time-driven.

stem: Which process controls the link between the project manager and the team manager?
options: Directing a project
Managing a stage boundary
Controlling a stage
Managing product delivery
explanation: Managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and the team manager by agreeing the requirements for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of specialist products.

stem: Which management product describes how and how often the project communicates with, and gets feedback from, its ecosystem?
options: Digital and data management approach
Highlight report
Communication management approach
Project brief
explanation: The communication management approach, part of the PID, sets the means and frequency of communication and feedback, giving a controlled two-way flow of information with stakeholders.

stem: Which role is accountable for the quality of the products delivered by the suppliers and for the project's technical integrity?
options: Senior user
Project assurance
Senior supplier
Executive
explanation: The senior supplier represents the supplier community, commits supplier resources and is accountable for the quality of products delivered by suppliers and for technical integrity.

stem: Which is a purpose of managing a stage boundary?
options: Giving users the final project product
Giving the business layer the project mandate
Giving the team manager the authority to start work on a new work package
Giving the board information to review the stage and plan the next
explanation: Managing a stage boundary gives the board enough information to review the current stage, approve the next stage plan, review the updated project plan and confirm continued justification and acceptable risks.

stem: In PRINCE2, who does the people element cover?
options: Only those named in the project management team structure
Only the staff of the organization paying for the project
Only the users who will receive the project's products
Those working on the project and those affected by it
explanation: People covers those working on the project and the relationships between them, as well as those impacted by the project, who may hold no formal role at all.

stem: Which is a factor that influences how PRINCE2 is tailored to a project?
options: The date the project mandate arrived
The capability of the project team
The names of the project board members
The number of principles to apply
explanation: The method is tailored to suit the project environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and level of risk. All seven principles are always applied; they are not reduced by tailoring.

stem: When is the outline business case first developed?
options: During initiation, as part of the PID
At the end of the first delivery stage
After the project closes, for post-project benefit reviews
In the pre-project period, during starting up a project
explanation: The outline business case is developed before the project starts, in starting up a project. It is refined into the full business case in the initiation stage and then maintained and updated through the stages.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 not plan every stage in detail at the start of the project?
options: Stage plans are written after the stage has finished
The project board does not approve detailed plans
Accurate planning is only possible for a limited time ahead
Detailed plans are only needed for projects with external suppliers
explanation: The planning horizon is the period for which it is possible to plan accurately. So the project plan stays high level, and each stage plan is produced near the end of the previous stage.

stem: Which record identifies all the quality control activities planned or carried out?
options: Issue register
Quality register
Product register
Lessons log
explanation: The quality register, part of the project log, identifies all quality control activities planned or done and feeds end stage and end project reports. The product register records the products and their acceptance.

stem: What is risk appetite?
options: The money set aside to fund the responses to threats and opportunities
The combined effect of all the project's threats and opportunities
The amount and type of risk the business will take for its objectives
The threshold for each objective beyond which risk is escalated
explanation: Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk the business is willing to take in pursuit of its objectives. Risk tolerance is the measurable threshold for each objective, and the risk budget is the money for responses.

stem: What is the project baseline?
options: The first version of the project plan, kept unchanged for later comparison
The set of tolerances agreed between the board and business
The list of products the project will hand over to users
The current approved versions of products that are under change control
explanation: The project baseline is the current approved versions of the management and specialist products that are subject to change control. A change is a modification to any of them.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is an exception?
options: A risk that has a high probability and impact
Any change to a product after it has been approved by the board
A forecast deviation beyond the agreed tolerance levels
A request from the board for more information
explanation: An exception is a situation where it can be forecast that there will be a deviation beyond the tolerance levels agreed between levels of management. It is raised on the forecast, before the breach.

stem: Which process provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed?
options: Managing a stage boundary
Directing a project
Closing a project
Controlling a stage
explanation: Closing a project provides a fixed point where acceptance of the project product is confirmed and the objectives, or approved changes to them, are recognized as achieved.

stem: A project team is made up of finance, IT and warehouse staff who will go back to their usual jobs when the new system goes live. Which TWO characteristics of a project does this show most clearly?
options: Temporary and cross-functional
Change and unique
Uncertain and cross-functional
Uncertain and temporary
explanation: Staff from several functions working together show the cross-functional characteristic, and the team ending at go-live shows that a project is temporary. Uniqueness and uncertainty are true of projects too, but the scenario does not describe them.

stem: Who is accountable for the project assurance of their own area of concern?
options: The project board members
The project manager
The project manager and team managers
Project support
explanation: Project board members are accountable for assurance of their respective areas: business assurance for the executive, user assurance for the senior user and supplier assurance for the senior supplier. Assurance is independent of the project manager.

stem: Why do project teams often need a different style of leadership from established business teams?
options: They never include external suppliers
They are larger than most business teams
They are temporary and cross organizational boundaries
They report directly to the business layer, not a line manager
explanation: Projects are delivered by temporary teams working across organizational boundaries, so a temporary leader may find it harder to exercise authority. Building trust and social cohesion matters more.

stem: When is managing a stage boundary NOT used for a planned stage end?
options: At the end of the initiation stage
At the end of the final stage
At the end of the second stage
At the end of a middle delivery stage
explanation: Managing a stage boundary is first used at the end of the initiation stage and repeated at the end of each later stage except the final one, which ends with closing a project. It can still be used in the final stage to prepare an exception plan.

stem:
Consider these statements about the PRINCE2 principles:

1. If the principles are not all applied, the project is not a PRINCE2 project.

2. The principles are guiding obligations and good practices.

3. A small project may leave out the principles it does not need.

4. The principles are a set of activities for the project manager.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: The principles are the guiding obligations and good practices that decide whether a project is genuinely managed with PRINCE2, so all seven must be applied. Activities belong to the processes, and tailoring adapts the method without dropping principles.

stem: Which management product defines the actions to confirm that the project's benefits are realized, including after the project closes?
options: Sustainability management approach
Benefits management approach
End project report
Project product description
explanation: The benefits management approach defines the management actions that ensure outcomes are achieved and confirm that benefits are realized. Many benefits come after closure, so it covers post-project reviews.

stem: What does a product flow diagram show?
options: The hierarchy of all the products to be produced during the plan
The sequence in which products are produced and their dependencies
The people responsible for producing each product
The costs, durations and resources needed for each product in turn
explanation: A product flow diagram shows the sequence of production and interdependencies of the products listed in the product breakdown structure. The hierarchy itself is the product breakdown structure.

stem: A product will not meet one of its quality specifications, and the project board accepts it without corrective action. What is this called?
options: An exception plan
A concession
A request for change
A quality review
explanation: An off-specification that the project board accepts without corrective action is a concession. A request for change proposes changing the baseline before the product is built.

stem: In the PRINCE2 risk technique, what happens in the assess step?
options: Planned risk responses are carried out and monitored
Risks are prioritized and the combined risk profile is assessed
The plan's context and objectives are reviewed to find new threats
Risk responses and monitoring arrangements are decided
explanation: The risk technique has identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate. Assess prioritizes risks and assesses the combined risk profile; plan decides the responses.

stem: In the PRINCE2 issue management technique, which step follows assess?
options: Capture
Decide
Implement
Recommend
explanation: The technique runs capture, assess, recommend, decide, implement. After the impact is assessed, options are identified and evaluated and a recommendation is made.

stem: Who sets the work package tolerances for a team manager?
options: The business layer
The project board
The project manager
The senior supplier
explanation: Tolerances are delegated down the levels: the business layer sets project tolerances, the board sets stage tolerances, and the project manager sets work package tolerances for team managers.

stem: Which organizational level sets the project tolerances and provides the project mandate?
options: The project manager
The project board
The team managers
The business layer
explanation: The commissioning party in the business layer provides the project mandate, identifies the executive and defines the project-level tolerances. The board directs within those, and sets stage tolerances for the project manager.

stem: How does PRINCE2 describe culture?
options: The organization's written policies and standards for projects
Shared attitudes, values, goals and ways of working of a group
The rules for how often reports go to the project board
The skills and experience of the project manager
explanation: Culture is the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and ways of working that characterize a group of people. Projects often cross several cultures, so cultural intelligence helps.

stem:
Consider these statements about starting up a project:

1. It confirms there is business justification for initiating the project.

2. It produces the full business case for authorizing the project.

3. It plans the work needed for the initiation stage.

4. It authorizes the project to deliver its products.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: Starting up a project confirms a business justification for initiating (the outline business case) and plans the initiation stage. The full business case is produced in initiating a project, and the board authorizes the project in directing a project.

stem: Why must the decision to start a project be explicit?
options: The project board meets only once in the project
The project mandate is only written after that decision has been made
The business case is only produced after closure
Starting up a project takes place before that decision is made
explanation: The activities in starting up a project happen before the decision to start, so the decision itself must be explicit. Starting up is pre-project; the project begins when the board authorizes initiation.

stem: What is the project ecosystem?
options: The organization's whole investment in all of its projects, programmes and other change
The business areas involved in or affected by the project, plus users and suppliers
The products and work packages delivered in a stage
The four levels of the project's management structure
explanation: The project ecosystem is those elements of the business involved in or directly impacted by the project and the associated users and suppliers. An organization's total investment in change is its portfolio.

stem: Which role is accountable for specifying the benefits and showing the business that they are on track to be realized?
options: Executive
Project manager
Senior user
Senior supplier
explanation: The senior user represents the user community, is accountable for capturing user requirements and specifying benefits aligned to the business case, and demonstrates that forecast benefits are on track.

stem: Before any work starts, the team writes a description of each product, including its quality specifications. Which principle does this apply?
options: Focus on products
Manage by exception
Manage by stages
Learn from experience
explanation: Focus on products means the project concentrates on defining and delivering products, in particular their user quality expectations and requirements. Product descriptions with quality specifications are how it is applied.

stem: What does the business case document?
options: The roles and reporting lines of the project management team
The way the project will be tailored to its environment
The products to be delivered and their quality specifications and acceptance criteria
The justification for the project, weighing costs, benefits and risks
explanation: The business case documents the business justification for the project, based on estimated costs against expected benefits, offset by associated risks, and how and when benefits can be measured.

stem: Which plan shows the major products of the project and when, how and at what cost they will be delivered?
options: Project plan
Team plan
Exception plan
Stage plan
explanation: The project plan is a high-level plan showing the major products of the project and when, how and at what cost they will be delivered.

stem: Where are the user's quality expectations for the project product recorded?
options: In the communication management approach
In the project product description
In each work package description
In the quality register
explanation: The user's quality expectations are a statement about the quality expected from the project product, captured in the project product description along with the acceptance criteria.

stem: How does PRINCE2 define a risk?
options: A forecast that a tolerance will be exceeded
An uncertain event that, if it occurs, will affect the objectives
An event that has already happened and needs management attention
A product that will not meet its quality specifications
explanation: A risk is an uncertain event or set of events that, should it occur, will affect the achievement of objectives. An event that has already happened and needs attention is an issue.

stem: How does PRINCE2 define an issue?
options: A product that has failed its quality review
A complaint raised by a stakeholder outside the project
An uncertain event that, if it occurs, may affect the project's objectives
An event relevant to the project that needs management consideration
explanation: An issue is an event relevant to the project that requires project management consideration. An uncertain event that may happen is a risk.

stem: Who produces a checkpoint report, and for whom?
options: Project assurance, for the executive
The project manager, for the project board
The project board, for the business layer
A team manager, for the project manager
explanation: A checkpoint report is a team-level, time-driven report from a team manager to the project manager on a work package, at a frequency set in the work package description.

stem: Which is an objective of directing a project?
options: Team managers know the expected effort and cost
Progress information reaches the project manager
The PID is assembled from the management approaches
There is authority to close the project
explanation: Directing a project ensures there is authority to initiate, to deliver and to close the project, gives management direction, keeps the project viable and connects it to the business layer.

stem: Users and key influencers help design a new process and agree how it will be used. What is this called?
options: Change control
Quality assurance
Co-creation
Stakeholder mapping
explanation: Co-creation is a form of collaboration that involves users and key influencers in designing products and agreeing ways of working, so the results are adopted. Change control handles changes to the baseline.

stem: How does PRINCE2 define a project?
options: A permanent team that runs and improves an organization's business as usual services each day
A temporary organization created to deliver business products to an agreed business case
A plan of activities with fixed start and end dates agreed by a sponsor
A set of related programmes managed together to meet strategic objectives
explanation: A project is a temporary organization created for the purpose of delivering one or more business products according to an agreed business case. A set of programmes and projects managed together is a portfolio.

stem: Which statement about project support is correct?
options: It is always provided by a permanent office
It must be kept separate from project assurance
It approves changes within the change budget
It is a responsibility of the senior supplier role
explanation: Project support is the project manager's responsibility, though it can be delegated. It must be kept separate from project assurance so assurance stays independent. A change authority, not support, approves changes.

stem: Which document is produced in initiating a project and used by the board to authorize the project?
options: The end project report
The project mandate
The full business case
The outline business case
explanation: Initiating a project produces the full business case, which the board uses to authorize the project and which is the basis for checking that the project remains viable. The outline business case comes from starting up.

stem: A project is planned, monitored and controlled one stage at a time, with the board deciding at each stage end whether to continue. Which principle is this?
options: Manage by exception
Focus on products
Ensure continued business justification
Manage by stages
explanation: Manage by stages means a PRINCE2 project is planned, monitored and controlled on a stage-by-stage basis. The board's decision point at each stage end is what gives it control.

stem: A council installs smart street lights (the project's product). Residents then feel safer walking at night. What is the residents feeling safer?
options: A business objective
A dis-benefit
An outcome
An output
explanation: The street lights are the output. An outcome is the result of the change, normally affecting real-world behaviour and circumstances, such as residents feeling safer. A measurable improvement from it would be a benefit.

stem: Which statement about team plans is correct?
options: They are approved by the business layer
They are optional in PRINCE2
They are produced before the project plan
They replace the stage plan for each stage
explanation: Team plans are used to organize and control a team's work on a work package, and they are optional in PRINCE2.

stem: Which part of the quality procedure monitors specific products to see if they comply with relevant standards?
options: Quality control
Quality planning
Quality tolerance
Quality assurance
explanation: Quality control monitors the specific products and their development to see whether they comply with standards, and finds ways to remove causes of poor performance. Quality planning captures the specifications first.

stem: Which record holds the identified risks for the project, with their status and history?
options: Daily log
Issue register
Lessons log
Risk register
explanation: The risk register, part of the project log, is the record of identified risks, including their status and history. The daily log is for informal problems and concerns.

stem: Testing shows a delivered product will not meet one of its agreed quality specifications. What type of issue is this?
options: A business opportunity
An off-specification
A request for change
A concern
explanation: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications. If the board then accepts it without corrective action, it becomes a concession.

stem: The project manager forecasts that a stage will exceed its cost tolerance. What should be sent to the project board?
options: A checkpoint report
An end stage report
An exception report
A highlight report
explanation: An exception report explains to the board where tolerances are, or are forecast to be, breached for the stage or project, and asks for direction. The board may then ask for an exception plan.

stem: Which part of the PID sets out how the project will help people move from the current state to the target state?
options: The change management approach
The issue management approach
The communication management approach
The quality management approach
explanation: PRINCE2 addresses change by creating and maintaining a change management approach in the PID. The communication management approach covers how information flows with stakeholders.

stem: Which process assigns work, monitors it, handles issues, reports to the board and takes corrective action to keep a stage within tolerance?
options: Controlling a stage
Managing a stage boundary
Managing product delivery
Directing a project
explanation: Controlling a stage assigns and monitors work, handles issues, reports progress to the board and takes corrective action to keep the stage within the tolerances set by the board.

stem: To whom does a team manager report?
options: The executive
The project board
The project manager
The senior supplier
explanation: The team manager is responsible for producing the products allocated in a work package and reports to, and takes direction from, the project manager.

stem: A group of warehouse staff has no role in the project but will use the new system every day. What should the project do?
options: Give them seats on the project board
Leave them out until the system is ready to be handed over
Ask the supplier to manage their concerns
Engage them as stakeholders affected by the change
explanation: Stakeholders include people impacted by the project who hold no formal role. Engaging them early supports adoption. Board seats are for the executive, senior user and senior supplier roles.

stem: Which principle requires a project to engage the business, user and supplier interests through agreed roles?
options: Focus on products
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Tailor to suit the project
Ensure continued business justification
explanation: This principle says a PRINCE2 project has defined and agreed roles and responsibilities in a structure that engages the business, user and supplier interests, and builds relationships with stakeholders.

stem: Which role is responsible for the business case and for the project's continued business justification?
options: Project manager
Senior supplier
Executive
Senior user
explanation: The executive secures funding and is responsible for the business case and continued business justification. The senior user specifies benefits and shows they are on track to be realized.

stem: For which level of plan is a project product description written?
options: Every team plan
Every stage plan
Every exception plan only
The project plan only
explanation: The project product description is written for the project plan only. Product breakdown structures, product descriptions and product flow diagrams are produced for every level of plan.

stem: Which management product describes the quality techniques and standards to be applied and who is responsible for achieving the required quality?
options: Quality management approach
Product description
Project product description
Quality register
explanation: The quality management approach, part of the PID, describes the quality techniques and standards and the roles and responsibilities for achieving quality and acceptance criteria.

stem: A project might finish early if a supplier delivers ahead of schedule, and the team acts to make that more likely. Which response is this?
options: Enhance
Share
Reduce
Exploit
explanation: Enhancing an opportunity makes it more likely or increases its effect. Exploiting acts to make sure the opportunity happens; reduce is the threat response that lowers probability or impact.

stem: When is an issue report created?
options: Only for issues that need to be handled formally
Only when a risk owner closes a risk
Only at the end of each management stage
For every issue, including those in the daily log
explanation: An issue report holds the description, impact assessment and recommendations for an issue. It is created only for issues handled formally.

stem: For which of these can tolerances be set in PRINCE2?
options: Number of stages
Sustainability
Team morale
Stakeholder numbers
explanation: Tolerances are set for the seven performance targets: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk.

stem: Which is an objective of managing product delivery?
options: The business case is updated for the end of the stage
Planned products are delivered to quality expectations and in tolerance
The project board has the authority it needs to deliver the project product
The previous stage is reviewed by the board
explanation: Managing product delivery ensures team work is authorized and agreed, teams know what to produce at what effort, cost and timescale, products meet quality expectations within tolerance, and progress is reported.

stem: Which helps build an effective project team under PRINCE2?
options: Choosing members only from the supplier organization
Diversity, matching capability to the work and building trust
Avoiding changes to agreed ways of working once set
Keeping members apart so that each one can work independently
explanation: Effective teams draw on diversity, the right capability and competence, and team building that creates trust and compatible ways of working, whether co-located, virtual or hybrid.

stem: What links the product breakdown structure to the work packages?
options: The project management team structure
The quality register
The work breakdown structure
The product flow diagram
explanation: The work breakdown structure is a hierarchy of all work to be done during a project and forms the link between the product breakdown structure and the work packages.

stem: Which process is used to prepare an exception plan?
options: Managing product delivery
Starting up a project
Managing a stage boundary
Controlling a stage
explanation: Managing a stage boundary is also used to prepare an exception plan and seek approval to replace the project or stage plan with it. This can happen at any time, including in the final stage.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is collaboration?
options: The project board meeting to approve a stage plan
Suppliers agreeing a contract with the commissioning business
People across the project ecosystem working together to the objectives
Team managers sending regular checkpoint reports to the project manager
explanation: Collaboration is people from across the project ecosystem working together to achieve the project's objectives. Co-creation is a specific form of it.

stem: Initiating a project ensures a common understanding of how the project applies business policies, methods and guidance. Which management product brings this initiation information together to gain authorization for the project?
options: The daily log
The lessons log
The communication management approach
The project initiation documentation
explanation: The project initiation documentation (PID) aggregates the management products created or updated during initiation, including how the project applies business policies, methods and guidance, and is used to gain authorization for the project to proceed. Logs are informal records kept by the project manager.

stem: What does the sustainability management approach define?
options: The suppliers allowed to work on the project
Actions, reviews and controls to meet sustainability targets
The environmental benefits that will help to pay for the project
The tolerance for the project's overall cost
explanation: The sustainability management approach defines the actions, reviews and controls that ensure the project's sustainability performance targets are achieved. It sits in the PID alongside the other management approaches.

stem: A project needs a new government standard to be published before it can finish one of its products. What kind of dependency is this?
options: External
Optional
Internal
Sequential
explanation: An external dependency is between a project product and a product or activity outside the project's scope, which the team cannot fully control. An internal dependency is between two products of the project.

stem: What does a product description include?
options: The names of the people who will accept the product
The product's purpose, composition and quality specifications
The risks and issues raised while the team was building the product
The product's cost, schedule and resource allocation
explanation: A product description describes a product's purpose, format, composition, derivation, quality specifications and development responsibilities. Costs and schedules are in plans.

stem: What does risk proximity describe?
options: How likely a risk is to occur
How near in time a risk might occur
How close a risk is to its tolerance
How quickly a risk would affect objectives
explanation: Risk proximity is how near in time a risk might occur. How quickly it would affect objectives once it occurs is risk velocity.

stem: What is a change budget?
options: The cost tolerance agreed for a stage
The total project budget approved by the board
Money set aside to fund planned responses to threats and opportunities
Money or authorized constraints set aside to cover changes
explanation: A change budget is the money or authorized constraints set aside in a plan to cover changes, allocated by those with delegated authority. Money for risk responses is the risk budget.

stem: Which log is an informal repository for lessons that apply to this project or to future projects?
options: Daily log
Lessons log
Quality register
Issue register
explanation: The lessons log is an informal repository for lessons. PRINCE2 has two logs, the daily log and the lessons log; the registers are records too, but they are kept formally.

stem: Which is an objective of closing a project?
options: Appointing the executive and project manager
Agreeing the work package with the team manager
Making provision for all open issues and risks
Preparing the stage plan for the next stage
explanation: Closing a project checks user acceptance, ensures the business can support the products, reviews performance against baselines, assesses benefits and makes provision for open issues and risks with follow-on action recommendations.

stem: A project builds a website by releasing a small working version, getting user feedback and then adding features in repeated cycles. Which delivery approach is this?
options: Hybrid
Iterative-incremental
Product-based delivery
Linear-sequential
explanation: Delivering in repeated cycles that each add to a working product is iterative-incremental. Linear-sequential finishes each step before the next starts; hybrid combines both. Product-based planning is a planning technique, not a delivery approach.

stem: On a small project, which role combination does PRINCE2 allow?
options: The project manager also doing the team manager role
Project support also doing project assurance
The executive also performing the project manager role
The project manager also doing user assurance
explanation: Depending on scale, the project manager may also perform the team manager and project support roles. The executive and project manager roles cannot be combined, and assurance must stay independent of the project manager and of support.

stem:
Consider these statements about communication in PRINCE2:

1. Communication is only needed with people who hold a project role.

2. Communication helps avoid misconceptions and needless barriers to change.

3. The communication management approach supports a two-way flow of information.

4. Remote and hybrid teams communicate in the same way as co-located teams.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
explanation: Communication avoids misconceptions and unnecessary barriers, and the communication management approach gives a controlled, bidirectional flow of information across the ecosystem. How teams communicate depends on whether they are co-located, remote or hybrid.

stem: The board decides to end a project early because it is no longer justified. What does closing a project make sure of?
options: The project is restarted with a new project manager
The work in progress is abandoned at once
All the remaining products are still finished and handed over as planned
The project is closed in an orderly way and value is salvaged
explanation: For a premature close, closing a project makes sure the project is closed in an orderly way and not simply abandoned, salvaging any value created and raising gaps left by the cancellation with the business.

stem:
Consider these statements about tailoring PRINCE2:

1. The executive and project manager roles can be combined on a small project.

2. Terms used in the method can be changed to match the organization's own.

3. One of the seven principles can be dropped for a low-risk project.

4. Tailoring adapts the method to the project's environment and complexity.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: Tailoring adapts the method, including its terminology, to suit the project environment, size and complexity. The principles are never dropped, and the executive role cannot be combined with the project manager role.

stem:
Consider these statements about the business case:

1. It is written once at start-up and then not changed.

2. It is checked at decision points such as stage boundaries.

3. It is only needed for projects funded by external customers.

4. It is maintained and updated as the project progresses.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: The business case is developed, then checked at key decision points and maintained through the project, with benefits confirmed during and after it. Every PRINCE2 project needs one, whoever funds it.

stem:
Consider these statements about stages:

1. A project has at least two stages.

2. Every project has exactly four stages.

3. The number of stages is set by the business layer.

4. The first stage is the initiation stage.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
explanation: There should be at least two stages, the first of which is the initiation stage. The number of stages varies with the nature of the products and the delivery activities; it is not fixed.

stem:
Consider these statements about quality roles:

1. The producer is the person or group who develops a product.

2. The approver must always be the senior supplier.

3. The reviewer is responsible for fixing defects found.

4. A reviewer is independent of the producer.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
explanation: The producer develops the product, and a reviewer is independent of the producer and assesses the product against its description. The approver can be any person or group qualified and authorized, such as the project board.

stem:
Consider these statements about the risk management approach:

1. It describes the procedure the project will use for managing risk.

2. It sets out roles and responsibilities for risk management.

3. It lists each risk with its status and history.

4. It is written by the senior supplier after each stage.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: The risk management approach, part of the PID, describes how risk will be managed, including the procedure, techniques, standards, responsibilities, tolerances and reporting. The list of risks and their history is the risk register.

stem:
Consider these statements about change control:

1. A request for change may be approved, rejected or deferred.

2. Only the project manager may decide on a request for change.

3. The board can delegate some change decisions to a change authority.

4. Changes to the baseline need no record once agreed.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: Change control identifies, assesses and then approves, rejects or defers changes to the baseline. The board can delegate authority for some changes to a change authority, and records and the baseline are updated when changes are implemented.

stem:
Consider these statements:

1. The PID is created during starting up a project and not updated.

2. The PID brings together key information to start the project on a sound basis.

3. The project log holds the daily log, lessons log and the registers.

4. The project log needs the board to agree its format.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
explanation: The PID is assembled during initiation and reviewed at stage boundaries. The project log holds the daily log, lessons log and the issue, product, quality and risk registers. Logs are informal and need no board agreement on format.

stem:
Consider these statements about the project board:

1. It manages the project on a day-to-day basis.

2. It sets the work package tolerances for team managers.

3. It is accountable to the business for the project's success.

4. It sets stage tolerances to manage by exception.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: The project board is accountable to the business for the project's success and sets stage tolerances. Day-to-day management and work package tolerances belong to the project manager.

stem: How does the people element relate to the other PRINCE2 elements?
options: It only applies during the closing a project process
It replaces the organizing practice on small and simple projects
The principles, practices and processes are applied by people
It is managed separately from the practices
explanation: People are central to the method: the principles, practices and processes are applied by the people involved. The organizing practice sets the roles, and the people element covers how those people work together and with those affected.

stem:
Consider these statements about the processes:

1. Managing product delivery is used only by the project board.

2. Initiating a project happens after the first delivery stage.

3. Starting up a project is used by both the directing and managing levels.

4. Closing a project is used for both a planned and a premature close.

Which two statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
explanation: Starting up a project is used by both the directing and managing levels, and closing a project handles both a planned close and a premature one. Managing product delivery is the team manager's process, and initiation is the first stage.

stem: Which is one of the seven PRINCE2 processes?
options: Planning the project
Reviewing benefits
Managing the business case
Managing a stage boundary
explanation: The seven processes are starting up a project, directing a project, initiating a project, controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary and closing a project.

stem: Which is one of the seven PRINCE2 principles?
options: Plan the whole project in detail
Tailor to suit the project
Use a single delivery method
Keep the project board informed weekly
explanation: The seven principles are ensure continued business justification, learn from experience, define roles, responsibilities and relationships, manage by stages, manage by exception, focus on products and tailor to suit the project.

stem: What does PRINCE2 say is needed to deliver the change that a project introduces?
options: A fixed-price contract
Effective leadership
A single delivery method
A large project board
explanation: Change management moves an organization from the current to the target state, and effective leadership is needed to deliver that change and bring people with it.

stem: Which is an example of a time-driven control?
options: An end stage report at the end of a stage
A highlight report sent every two weeks
An exception report after a forecast breach
An end project report at closure
explanation: Time-driven controls take place at predefined periodic intervals, such as highlight and checkpoint reports. End stage, exception and end project reports are triggered by events.

stem: When is an exception plan produced?
options: At the start of every stage, alongside the stage plan
After an exception report, to show how the project will respond
When a team manager accepts a work package
When the project is closed early and needs a plan for closing it
explanation: An exception plan follows an exception report and explains how the project will respond to the exception. Once approved, it replaces the plan that was in exception.

stem: How does PRINCE2 define quality?
options: The degree to which a product was delivered on time
The agreement of the users that they like the finished product overall
The absence of any defects in the finished product
The degree to which inherent characteristics fulfil requirements
explanation: Quality is the degree to which a set of inherent characteristics of a product, service, process, person, organization, system or resource fulfils its requirements.

stem: A risk is written as: 'Because the venue has no backup generator, a power cut may stop the event, delaying the launch.' What is 'a power cut may stop the event'?
options: The risk response
The risk cause
The risk effect
The risk event
explanation: Describing a risk by cause, event and effect separates the source (no backup generator), the uncertain event (a power cut stopping the event) and the effect on objectives (a delayed launch).

stem: Which type of issue has an immediate and negative impact?
options: A concern
A problem
A request for change
An off-specification
explanation: A problem is an issue with an immediate and negative impact. A concern is an issue whose timeliness and impact still need to be assessed.

stem: What is a business objective?
options: A limit on how much a plan may deviate before escalation
A task the project manager must complete in each stage
A measurable outcome showing progress toward the organization's strategy
A product that the project must deliver to gain the users' formal acceptance
explanation: Business objectives are the measurable outcomes that demonstrate progress against the organization's strategy, to which the project should contribute through its benefits.

stem: Within what does the project manager run the project on behalf of the project board?
options: The agreed project tolerances and constraints
The risk appetite of the senior supplier
The work package tolerances set by team managers
The budget agreed with project support
explanation: The project manager has authority to run the project day to day on behalf of the board within the agreed tolerances and constraints, and sets work package tolerances for team managers.

stem: Which is one of the seven aspects of project performance that PRINCE2 manages?
options: Morale
Innovation
Stakeholder satisfaction
Sustainability
explanation: The seven aspects of performance are benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk. Each has its own tolerance. Morale and reputation matter, but they are not performance targets in the method.

stem: What triggers starting up a project?
options: The project mandate
The first highlight report
The project initiation documentation
The project brief
explanation: The project mandate is produced by the authority commissioning the project, in the business layer, and is the trigger for starting up a project. The project brief is an output of starting up.

stem: When should a PRINCE2 project team look for and apply lessons?
options: Only after the project has been closed
At the start, throughout the project and at its close
Only when an exception has been raised
Only during starting up a project and initiating a project
explanation: Learn from experience applies across the whole lifecycle: lessons from earlier projects are sought at the start, lessons are recorded and applied during the project, and they are passed on at the end.

stem: A project team includes staff from three countries who work in quite different ways. Which ability helps most?
options: Risk appetite
Product-based planning
Cultural intelligence
Quality control
explanation: Cultural intelligence is the ability to relate and work across cultures within the organizational ecosystem. It helps a mixed team find compatible ways of working.

stem: Which report gives the project board the project's performance during a stage and its status at the stage end?
options: End stage report
Highlight report
Checkpoint report
Lessons report
explanation: The end stage report is given by the project manager to the board at the end of each stage, with performance during the stage and status at its end.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is a schedule?
options: The record of the time-driven reports sent to the project board
A list of the products to be produced during a plan
A description of a product's quality specifications
A graphical representation of a plan, such as a Gantt chart
explanation: A schedule is a graphical representation of a plan, such as a Gantt chart, typically showing a sequence of tasks with resource allocations.

stem: What happens during quality planning?
options: Finished products are tested against standards
Users formally accept the project product
Independent checks confirm the project is being run correctly
Quality specifications are captured in product descriptions
explanation: Quality planning captures the quality specifications for the project products and produces the associated product descriptions and quality management approach. Testing finished products is quality control.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 call risk exposure a neutral concept?
options: It is measured only after the project closes
Exposure can be positive or negative
It does not depend on probability or impact
It is set by the business, not the project
explanation: Risk exposure is the degree to which an objective is at risk. It is neutral because exposure can be positive, from opportunities, or negative, from threats.

stem: A team finds that a component it built can also be sold to another department, a positive result nobody expected. What type of issue is this?
options: A business opportunity
A concession
A request for change
A newly identified opportunity risk
explanation: A business opportunity is an issue that represents previously unanticipated positive consequences for the project or user organization. It has already been found, so it is an issue rather than a risk.

stem: Which is an objective of starting up a project?
options: Work packages are authorized for each team
The full business case is approved by the project board before initiation
Products are handed over to the users
Alternative approaches are evaluated and the project approach agreed
explanation: Starting up evaluates alternative approaches and agrees the chosen project approach, alongside the outline business case, authorities, project brief, appointments and the initiation stage plan.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is an output?
options: The tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity
The measurable improvement from an outcome
The completed set of project outputs needed for an outcome
The result of change in real-world behaviour
explanation: An output is the tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity. The completed set of outputs needed to deliver an outcome is a capability.

stem: The project board delegates the review of small requests for change to a nominated group with a budget. What is this group called?
options: A project assurance team
A project office
Project support
A change authority
explanation: A change authority is a person or group to which the board may delegate responsibility for considering requests for change or off-specifications. It may be given a change budget and approve changes within it.

stem: Why does a project need a different management approach from business as usual?
options: It never affects the people who do the day-to-day work
It must always be run by an external supplier
It is temporary, cross-functional and brings change with uncertainty
It always costs more than the organization spends on running its operations
explanation: Projects bring change, are temporary and cross-functional, are unique and carry uncertainty, so they need management that differs from running the business. Many projects are internal and nearly all affect the people doing business as usual.

stem: What does the business justification principle require of a project?
options: A justification reviewed only when the project closes
A justification written only for projects with external suppliers
A justification to start and an ongoing one to its completion
A justification approved once by the business before start-up
explanation: The principle needs business justification sufficient to warrant investment to initiate the project and ongoing investment through to completion. If it is lost, the project should be stopped.

stem: What does PRINCE2 say a project's performance depends on?
options: The seniority of the people on the project board
The number of management products the project produces
How closely the project team follows the whole method without any tailoring
The team's capability, its relationships and the people the change affects
explanation: How well change is implemented, and so how well the project performs, depends on the capabilities of the team, the strength of their relationships and the people affected by the change.

stem: Which report confirms the handover of all products and reviews how the project performed?
options: Highlight report
Lessons report for the business
End stage report
End project report
explanation: The end project report goes from the project manager to the board, confirming the handover of all products, reviewing performance and requesting approval to close.

stem: Initiating a project aims to give a common understanding of several things. Which is one of them?
options: When the next stage boundary will be reached
Which products the team will build this week
How progress will be monitored and controlled
Whether there is a viable and worthwhile project
explanation: Initiating a project aims for common understanding of the reasons, scope, delivery, decision-making, quality, baselines, risks and issues, how progress is monitored and controlled, information needs and how business policies are applied.

stem: Which planning product is a hierarchy of all the products to be produced during a plan?
options: Work breakdown structure
Product flow diagram
Project product description
Product breakdown structure
explanation: A product breakdown structure is a hierarchy of all the products to be produced during a plan. The work breakdown structure covers the work to produce them.

stem: Which part of the project log identifies the products to be delivered and records their acceptance?
options: Issue register
Product register
Quality register
Risk register
explanation: The product register is a component of the project log that identifies the products the project will deliver and records their acceptance.

stem: What is a risk budget?
options: Money to pay for the risk management approach itself
Money to cover changes to the approved baseline
Money to fund responses to the project's threats and opportunities
Money kept back by the business to cover any project overspend
explanation: A risk budget is a sum of money to fund specific responses to threats and opportunities, such as the cost of contingent plans. Money for changes is the change budget.

stem: Who should monitor the issue register on a regular basis?
options: The senior user
The project assurance team
The project manager
The team manager
explanation: The issue register captures and maintains information on all issues managed formally, and it should be monitored by the project manager regularly.

stem: In which process is the project initiation documentation assembled?
options: Managing a stage boundary
Initiating a project
Starting up a project
Directing a project
explanation: The PID is assembled in initiating a project from the management products created or updated during initiation, and it is used to gain authorization for the project to proceed.

stem: Which management product supports the business case practice by giving the project a well-defined starting point?
options: The checkpoint report
The quality register
The issue register
The project brief
explanation: The project brief, created in starting up a project, gives the project a commonly understood and well-defined starting point. It is superseded by the PID and not maintained.

stem: Which part of the PID describes the organizational and commercial arrangements with suppliers?
options: The commercial management approach
The communication management approach
The benefits management approach
The quality management approach
explanation: The commercial management approach supports the organizing practice by describing the delivery model: the organizational and commercial arrangements, reflected in the project management team structure.

stem: Manage by exception establishes limits of delegated authority. What are those limits called?
options: Baselines
Tolerances
Constraints
Milestones
explanation: Manage by exception defines tolerances for performance against plans. Each level of management can act freely inside its tolerances and escalates when a forecast says they will be exceeded.

stem: Why does a project affect people's business as usual?
options: It takes over business as usual work while it runs
It replaces the organization's normal line management structure for good
It needs the users to stop work until handover
It delivers change to their activities, routines and responsibilities
explanation: The purpose of a project is to deliver change, and that change affects people in their business as usual activities, routines and responsibilities.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is a forecast?
options: A prediction made by studying historical data and past patterns
A record of the products accepted so far
A plan that replaces the current stage plan after an exception occurs
A target set by the business for the project
explanation: A forecast is a prediction made by studying historical data and past patterns. Forecasting the remaining work lets the project manager spot an exception before it happens.

stem: Which feature of PRINCE2 means it can be used for any project, of any scale, alongside industry-specific models?
options: Outcome-focused
Universal
Proven
Common language
explanation: PRINCE2 is universal: it can be applied to any project of any scale and used alongside specialist models. Proven refers to its basis in established practice, and common language to the shared vocabulary it gives everyone.

stem: In the PRINCE2 planning technique, what comes after defining and analysing the products?
options: Creating the product breakdown structure
Organizing work packages
Writing product descriptions
Writing the project product description
explanation: After the products are defined and analysed, the technique goes on to organizing work packages, preparing estimates, preparing the schedule, analysing risks, preparing the budget and documenting the plan.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is a requirement?
options: A contract term agreed with an external supplier
A limit on cost that must not be exceeded
A wish from a user that has not yet been written down or agreed
A need or expectation documented in an approved management product
explanation: A requirement is a need or expectation that is documented in an approved management product. Until it is documented and approved it is not a requirement under the method.

stem: What is residual risk?
options: A risk left over from a previous project
A risk that has already occurred and turned into an issue
The risk remaining after a response has been applied
A risk that nobody has been assigned to own
explanation: Residual risk is the risk remaining after the risk response has been applied. A risk that has occurred is managed as an issue.

stem: In the decide step of the issue technique, which is a possible decision?
options: Register the issue
Determine the issue type
Ask for an exception plan
Assess impact on the business case
explanation: In the decide step the decision-maker can approve, reject, ask for an exception plan or request more information. Registering the issue and determining its type happen at capture.

stem: When should managing a stage boundary be carried out?
options: Only when an exception is raised
Only after the final stage
At, or close to, the end of each stage
At the start of every work package in a stage
explanation: Managing a stage boundary should be executed at, or close to, the end of each stage so the board can review the stage and decide on the next. It is also used for exception plans.

stem: A project board asks for a detailed report every day and approves every small decision itself. Which principle is it failing to apply?
options: Focus on products
Manage by stages
Learn from experience
Manage by exception
explanation: Under manage by exception the board delegates within tolerances and is involved when a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded. Approving every small decision makes poor use of the board's time and the project manager's authority.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is management?
options: Instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working
Setting the project-level tolerances on behalf of the commissioning business
Motivating people to achieve the project's objectives
Approving the business case at each stage boundary
explanation: Management is instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working. Motivating people to achieve objectives is leadership.

stem: Which management product supports the progress practice by describing how the project will manage its data and digital tools?
options: Change management approach
Digital and data management approach
Commercial management approach
Communication management approach for reporting
explanation: The digital and data management approach, part of the PID, supports progress management, including the use of data and systems to monitor and report progress.

stem: Most benefits of a training programme will only be seen a year after the project closes. How does PRINCE2 handle this?
options: Recording them as dis-benefits in the risk register
Post-project benefit reviews in the benefits management approach
Keeping the whole project open until every benefit has been measured
Removing those benefits from the business case
explanation: Benefits that come after closure are confirmed through post-project reviews planned in the benefits management approach, which is updated during closing a project. The project is not kept open to wait for them.

stem: When does PRINCE2 use the term 'customer'?
options: For the executive on every project
Whenever the users are outside the business
For anyone at all who will use the project's products after handover
Only where there is a commercial relationship with the supplier
explanation: The term customer is only used where there is a commercial relationship between the business and the supplier. It is the person or group from the business who commissioned the work and will benefit from the results.

stem: Which is an objective of managing a stage boundary?
options: Producing the project brief for the board
Agreeing tolerances for each work package
Confirming that the project product is accepted by the users
Recording lessons that can help later stages or other projects
explanation: Managing a stage boundary assures the board the stage is complete, prepares the next stage or exception plan, updates the PID, informs the board on viability, records lessons and requests authorization to continue.

stem: How does PRINCE2 define the scope of a plan?
options: The list of users who will receive the products from each stage plan
The money set aside in a plan to cover changes
The product, delivery and management activities in an approved plan
The period over which the benefits are realized
explanation: Scope is the sum of the product, delivery and management activities represented by an approved plan and its product and work package descriptions. Money set aside for changes is the change budget.

stem: What are quality specifications?
options: The quality measures and the levels a finished product must meet
The independent checks the business makes on the project
The prioritized list of criteria for accepting the project product
The user's general statement of the quality they expect
explanation: Quality specifications describe the quality measures that will be applied by those performing quality control and the levels the finished product must meet.

stem: The team cannot prevent a key supplier going out of business, so it agrees in advance what it will do if that happens. Which response is this?
options: Avoid the threat
Transfer the risk to a third party
Prepare contingent plans
Accept the risk
explanation: Preparing contingent plans means planning in advance the actions to take if the risk occurs. Accepting is a decision to take no action and live with the risk.

stem: When should the project manager escalate an issue to the project board?
options: Whenever any issue is entered in the daily log
When resolving it would go beyond the project manager's authority
Only when the issue is raised by a team manager
