Only once the stage has already gone beyond its agreed tolerances
explanation: In the recommend step, an issue is escalated if dealing with it is beyond the project manager's delegated authority. Escalation is triggered by a forecast, before tolerances are exceeded.

stem: During a stage, the project manager needs advice on a difficult decision from the project board. Which process covers the board's response?
options: Managing a stage boundary
Directing a project
Initiating a project
Controlling a stage
explanation: Directing a project gives appropriate management direction and control throughout the project's life, including responding to requests for advice from the project manager.

stem: A project is small, low-risk and run by an experienced team. Under the tailor to suit the project principle, what should happen?
options: The method is applied exactly as written, whatever the scale
The project is run without any PRINCE2 practices
The principles are reduced to the four most useful
The method is adapted to fit the project's scale and risk
explanation: Tailoring adapts the method to the project's environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and risk. A small project still applies all seven principles and all the practices, in a lighter form.

stem: Who must a project involve, according to the people element?
options: Those with project roles and key people affected by or critical to it
Only those named in the project management team structure
Only the executive, the senior user and the senior supplier on the board
Only staff of the business that pays for the project
explanation: A project needs to involve those with a formal role and key people who are either impacted by or critical to its success, even if they have no formal role.

stem: A team manager forecasts that a work package will exceed its time tolerance. What should the team manager do?
options: Change the work package tolerances
Raise an issue with the project manager
Send an exception report to the project board
Wait until the tolerance has been exceeded
explanation: Tolerance breaches are escalated one level up. For a work package, the team manager raises an issue with the project manager, who sets those tolerances. Exception reports go from the project manager to the board.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is project management?
options: Approving the business case before any work starts
Applying methods, tools, techniques and competencies to a project
Delivering the specialist products of a project to the users on time
Setting the overall objectives and tolerances for a project
explanation: PRINCE2 defines project management as the application of methods, tools, techniques and competencies to a project. Setting overall objectives and tolerances is done by the business layer.

stem: Why should a project's products be aligned to business objectives?
options: So the supplier can set the project's costs
So the project needs no tolerances for benefits
So the project board does not need to review progress at stage ends
So the outputs lead to outcomes and benefits the business wants
explanation: Products lead to outcomes, and outcomes to benefits that contribute to business objectives. Aligning products to those objectives, within tolerances, is part of managing the business case.

stem: Which management product describes the specific responsibilities of each member of the project management team?
options: Work package description
Project brief
Role descriptions
Lessons report
explanation: Role descriptions, part of the PID, describe the roles of those in the project management team and their specific responsibilities. A role is the function in this project, not a person's job outside it.

stem: What happens to the business case while a stage is being controlled?
options: It is replaced by the stage plan
It is written in full for the first time
It is left unchanged until closure
It is kept under review
explanation: Controlling a stage keeps the business case under review during the stage, as well as focusing on delivering the stage's products and controlling risks and issues.

stem: How do plans use tolerances?
options: To set the exact date when every product must be delivered
To remove the need to report progress until the end
To let team managers approve changes to the baseline
To give each level room to manage within its constraints
explanation: Plans use tolerances to manage constraints: each level can manage within its tolerances, giving flexibility, and escalates only when a forecast says they will be exceeded.

stem: Which type of acceptance is given by the group that will support a product after it goes into the operational environment?
options: Supplier acceptance of the delivered product
Project board approval at closure
User acceptance after handover
Operational and maintenance acceptance
explanation: Operational and maintenance acceptance is given by those who will support the product once delivered. User acceptance comes from those who will use it.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 ask teams to understand decision bias when managing risk?
options: Bias sets the business's risk appetite
Bias is recorded in the register in place of risk probability
Bias can distort how people identify and assess risks
Bias decides who becomes the risk owner
explanation: Risk culture and decision bias affect how people see and judge risk. Understanding bias helps a team identify and assess risks more objectively.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is change control?
options: Identifying, assessing and approving, rejecting or deferring baseline changes
Moving an organization from its current state to a target state
Recording the minor concerns that the project manager can handle informally
Assigning work packages to team managers for delivery
explanation: Change control is the process by which changes that may affect the project baseline are identified, assessed and then approved, rejected or deferred. Moving to a target state is change management.

stem: The focus on products principle concentrates on the definition and delivery of products, in particular their:
options: Risks and issues
Costs and dates of delivery
User quality expectations and requirements
Supplier contracts and commercial arrangements
explanation: A PRINCE2 project focuses on the definition and delivery of products, in particular their user quality expectations and requirements. Costs, dates and risks are planned around those products.

stem: A hybrid team rarely meets in person and members feel disconnected. What should the project manager focus on?
options: Raising an exception report to the project board
Building social cohesion and trust in the team
Moving the work into a single work package
Asking project assurance to take over the team
explanation: Bringing teams together and building social cohesion, whether co-located, virtual or hybrid, is part of managing successful teams. An exception report is for forecast tolerance breaches.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is a lesson?
options: A request to the project board for its approval to close the project at the end
A minor problem or concern that the project manager handles informally in the daily log
A quality check carried out on a specialist product during a stage of the project
Information that helps this or other projects and promotes learning
explanation: A lesson is information to facilitate the future of the project or other projects and actively promote learning from experience. The experience may be positive or negative. Lessons are kept informally in the lessons log.

stem: Which objective of directing a project continues past the end of the project?
options: There is authority to deliver the project product in each stage
The business layer is linked to the project
The project remains viable at each stage
Plans for realizing post-project benefits are managed and reviewed
explanation: Directing a project ensures plans for realizing post-project benefits are managed and reviewed. Benefits often come after closure, so the reviews are planned before the project ends.

stem: A project is part of a programme, uses an external supplier under contract and must meet strict environmental targets. Which integrated element of PRINCE2 covers these circumstances?
options: The organizing practice
The people
The project context
The processes
explanation: The project context is the element that covers the organizational and commercial setting, the delivery method, sustainability requirements and scale. The principles, practices and processes are then applied to fit that context.

stem: Where is benefits tolerance documented?
options: In the work package description
In the daily log
In the stage plan
In the business case
explanation: Benefits tolerance, the permissible deviation in benefit performance targets before escalation, is documented in the business case. Sustainability tolerance is documented there too.

stem: What is the difference between being accountable and being responsible in PRINCE2?
options: Neither can be delegated once the project starts
Responsibility cannot be delegated; accountability can
Both can be delegated to the project manager
Accountability cannot be delegated; responsibility can
explanation: The accountable person is the single person who owns a task, and accountability cannot be delegated. The responsible person has the authority and is expected to perform the task, and responsibility can be delegated.

stem: How does the plans practice support sustainability?
options: By planning how sustainability targets will be met in delivery
By moving all sustainability work until after the project has closed
By treating sustainability as a dis-benefit
By leaving sustainability to the supplier's own plans
explanation: Delivery sustainability is part of effective planning: plans show how the sustainability performance targets for the project work and products will be achieved.

stem: What does a quality review assess?
options: Whether a product is complete, meets standards and its specifications
Whether the team is working to agreed ways of working
Whether the stage will finish inside its tolerances
Whether the project is still fully justified by its business case
explanation: Quality reviews assess whether a product is complete, adheres to standards and meets its quality specifications. They may happen at several points in a complex product's development.

stem: What is risk tolerance?
options: The chance that a given risk will occur at some point during the current stage
The amount and type of risk the business is willing to take overall
The length of time between a risk occurring and its effect being felt
A measurable threshold for the tolerable range of outcomes per objective
explanation: Risk tolerance is a measurable threshold for the tolerable range of outcomes for each objective at risk, in the same units used to measure that objective. Risk appetite is the business's overall willingness to take risk.

stem: Which management product describes how issues will be handled and changes controlled on the project?
options: The communication management approach
The issue register
The issue management approach
The risk management approach
explanation: The issue management approach, part of the PID, describes the procedures, techniques and responsibilities for handling issues and change control. The issue register records the issues themselves.

stem: A new project manager is not sure who should approve a change and whether the senior supplier can commit resources. Which principle has been poorly applied?
options: Ensure continued business justification
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Focus on products
Learn from experience
explanation: When people do not know who decides what, roles and responsibilities have not been defined and agreed. This principle makes accountability and authority clear across the business, user and supplier interests.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 want information to flow both ways between the project and its stakeholders?
options: It keeps users from changing their requirements
It lets the project board approve every decision in person
Feedback supports alignment and helps shape the project
It removes the need for highlight reports
explanation: The communication management approach establishes a controlled, bidirectional flow so feedback from across the ecosystem keeps people aligned and helps shape the project.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is a dashboard?
options: A plan showing every product and its dependencies
A graphic summary of key decision-support data on progress
A formal report that replaces the highlight report each week
A list of open issues sorted by priority
explanation: A dashboard represents large amounts of decision-support data as a current, easy-to-read summary, usually graphic, of key information on progress and performance.

stem: Which document is used in managing product delivery to pass responsibility for work formally to a team manager?
options: Work package description
Product flow diagram
Team plan for the work
Project brief
explanation: A work package description describes how one or more products will be produced and delivered, and is used to pass responsibility for the work formally to a team manager or team member.
